clue.text: Be safe and lucky — after working in the garden?

explanation.surface: Someone muses on the good fortune of escaping trouble while digging the borders.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: after gardening, the soil (the land) ends up on your shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to come out of trouble unharmed by good fortune; read literally, earth clings to a gardener's boots.

clue.text: Female's friend is a target for abuse

parts.note: an aunt is a female relative; the possessive gives the S
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A woman's companion is picked on by everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: AUNT SALLY is a British fairground and pub game where players throw sticks at a dummy's head, hence anyone set up to be attacked.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used figuratively for any person or idea put up to be criticised or ridiculed.

clue.text: Act for each drug addict

parts.note: to do is to act or perform
per means for each, as in 'per head'

explanation.surface: Someone stands in for every user of narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A user of illegal stimulants or narcotics, especially a sports cheat, is called this slang term.

clue.text: Foul knock for a boxer, or a hurricane for a sailor

explanation.surface: A fighter's illegal punch is compared with the storm a seaman fears.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's punch is a vicious hit; to a seaman, the phrase means a fierce gale.

clue.text: Melon-like fruit rushed up as follows

indicators.note: follows says the word as comes after the turned piece
in a down clue, 'up' means the word for rushed is written bottom to top

parts.note: ran means rushed

explanation.surface: A fruit resembling a melon is described as having sped upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The narras is a southern African desert shrub bearing a prickly fruit like a melon.

clue.text: For tram to follow and divert

explanation.surface: A transport planner sets out a route for a tram and a diversion.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch line off the main rails is one a tram may run along; as a verb the term means distract or deflect.

clue.text: An era or a century with' hope arising all round

indicators.note: all round says the turned word encloses the century letter
in a down clue, 'arising' means the word hope is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred, a century

explanation.surface: Someone describes a historical age, a hundred years filled with rising optimism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns HOPE into EPOH, and 'all round' places C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An age or period of history marked by notable events is an era.

clue.text: To deal on credit entirely …

parts.note: to tally is an old sense meaning to trade on credit, the tally stick recording the debt

explanation.surface: A trader buys and sells wholly on account.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next, which refers back to its word 'credit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean completely or wholly.

clue.text: … or the same thing could be triced

indicators.note: could be says the letters of triced might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue, the writer suggests the same item might have been hoisted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the same thing' points back to the word 'credit' in the previous clue; 'triced' (hoisted and tied) is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The previous clue ends with 'credit', so 'the same thing' names that word.

clue.text: What a bowler has to make hastily

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler is described as having to produce something in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a bowler takes a running approach to the crease before delivering the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler's approach run is called this; as a verb it also means to sew or build something quickly.

clue.text: Increase one's pace, being vigorous about a journey

indicators.note: about says the word for vigorous goes around the word for a journey

parts.note: stout means strong and vigorous
a ride is a journey on horseback or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: A walker speeds up, full of energy on an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen one's steps and walk briskly is the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Ruin some French weights used for gold, etc.

parts.note: des is French for 'some'
troy weight is the system used for precious metals and gems

explanation.surface: A jeweller's French measures spoil the gold.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreck or demolish something completely.

clue.text: A small bag found in converted chalets

indicators.note: converted means the letters of chalets are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone finds a little bag inside holiday cabins that have been remodelled.
explanation.definitionFit: A school bag with a shoulder strap is a small bag of this kind.

clue.text: Part of state licence expressing purpose

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of an official permit states what it is for.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a clause showing aim or end is so described, from Greek telos, an end.

clue.text: Telephone one dandy to cancel something

parts.note: to call is to telephone
I is the Roman numeral for one
a toff is a smart, well-dressed gentleman

explanation.surface: Someone rings a fashionable gent to call off an event.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to abandon a planned event.

clue.text: Having a slight swing, balance goes to Conservative

parts.note: Libra, the scales, is the zodiac sign of the balance
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Political commentary: the balance of power tips towards the Conservatives with a small electoral swing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swing' and 'balance' suggest an election; the definition is about oscillation.
explanation.definitionFit: Libration is a gentle oscillation, so the adjective describes something that sways slightly.

clue.text: Mount a fox's head for an Italian rustic dance

parts.note: berg is a mountain, as in German and South African place names
in hunting, a fox's head is called its mask

explanation.surface: Someone mounts a stuffed fox's head as a hunting trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a verb but supplies the noun BERG.
explanation.definitionFit: The bergamask, named after Bergamo, is a clownish country dance, as in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Off the mains and on in a quiet period

parts.note: taken as written
the main is a poetic word for the open sea, so the mains are seas

explanation.surface: Power cuts and restorations are described as a lull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mains' suggests electricity supply, but it is the old word for oceans.
explanation.definitionFit: The slack months for tourism or trade, when business is quiet.

clue.text: Possibly a river ship

parts.note: may expresses possibility
a river flows, so it can be called a 'flower'

explanation.surface: A sailor wonders whether a vessel is a river boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' here is pronounced flow-er, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620.

clue.text: Found a counterpart to a lighter edition

parts.note: a match is something used to light a fire

explanation.surface: A collector pairs a cigarette lighter with a newer version.
explanation.definitionFit: To pair something with its equal or twin.

clue.text: Former South African upset fakir

indicators.note: upset means the letters of fakir are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A holy man from the old Cape is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: This word is now an offensive racial slur in South Africa; older dictionaries recorded it for the Xhosa people.
explanation.definitionFit: Old dictionaries used the term for a Black South African of the Xhosa group; it is now a slur and banned.

clue.text: Go back to soak a vessel

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax or hemp to soften it
an urn is a vase or container

explanation.surface: Someone returns to steep a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To come again to a place.

clue.text: Marking bedding material

explanation.surface: A teacher checks work and a mattress is covered in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking with check marks; also a strong striped cotton used for mattress covers.

clue.text: Transport motor, vehicle on railway

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the car sits above the railway piece

parts.note: a car is a motor vehicle

explanation.surface: A car is loaded on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear or convey something from place to place.

clue.text: Direct a pilot

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be steered by a trained navigator.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer or lead; a pilot is one who leads the way.

clue.text: Old, like Coleridge's mariner

explanation.surface: Someone describes a sailor from a famous poem as aged.
explanation.definitionFit: Very old; Coleridge wrote The Rime of the Ancient Mariner.

clue.text: Virginian quail left in a bit' of change

indicators.note: in says the letter for left is placed inside the word for a small piece of money

parts.note: a coin is a piece of loose change

explanation.surface: A small American game bird is left inside a piece of loose change.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Virgilian' and 'bit''; the answer is a North American bird, so 'Virginian' is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The colin is the bobwhite, a quail native to Virginia and eastern North America.

clue.text: Instrument creating injury on one accountant

parts.note: harm means injury
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A tool is used to wound a bookkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: The mouth organ is a small musical instrument.

clue.text: Type of beam for cutting juice from frankincense

explanation.surface: A beam cuts through gum resin.
explanation.definitionFit: An intense light beam used in surgery and industry; also an old word for a gum resin from silphium.

clue.text: Michaelmas is one time for judgment

explanation.surface: The autumn feast is described as the moment of reckoning.
explanation.walkthrough: Michaelmas, 29 September, is an English quarter day when rents and accounts fell due.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter day settles accounts; the phrase also means the Last Judgement or any moment of retribution.
